Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Two readers can hold up the very same line from the book to prove opposite things. How?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
📖Reading: I will tell a thesis from a fact, a question, or a vague statement, and test evidence against a claim and against the other side.
✏️Grammar: I will check the verbs and commas in my own thesis.
📝Writing: I will revise my thesis and its reason, then turn in Week 2.

The Law of the Jungle
Rudyard Kipling (1895) · from “The Law of the Jungle,” lines 35–38 of 38
· · ·
Because of his age and his cunning, because of his gripe and his paw, In all that the Law leaveth open, the word of the Head Wolf is Law. Now these are the Laws of the Jungle, and many and mighty are they; But the head and the hoof of the Law and the haunch and the hump is—Obey!
· · ·
gripe: grip; an old spelling · leaveth open: leaves undecided · haunch: the hip and thigh · hump: the back · the head and the hoof: the whole of it, from one end to the other
★Buck’s team has a Head Wolf too. Who holds that place?

Step 2 · Claim A. Tap a gravel card, then tap the bin where it belongs.
CLAIM AThe North sets Buck free: it wakes strength and senses that the Southland had kept asleep.
Step 3 · Same gold, other claim. The cards that are in the book come back to the tray.
CLAIM BThe North destroys who Buck was: it wears away the fair and trusting dog from the Southland.
Stamped out: not in the book
Find a card that was pay dirt for one claim and fool’s gold for the other. What does that tell you about choosing evidence for your own thesis?
  • All seven notices are stamped.
  • All eight cards are sorted for Claim A.
  • All five cards are sorted again for Claim B.
  • You explained what the changed card tells you.

Verbs and commas in your own thesis
Professor Lovelore At the board
0:34
An AI-generated character and voice.
Weak or strong
Buck is different.→The trail hardens Buck’s muscles.
One · Ask the verb
The trail hardens what?→Muscles.
Two · Swap is and was
Buck was a thief.→Buck stole the bacon.
Three · Check your commas
After a long opener, a comma.→Around an interrupter, a pair.

Four lenses for your draft
  1. Arguable. Someone could take the other side.
  2. Specific. Exact words, not a lot, different, or things.
  3. Provable. Your reason rests on a cited moment from Chapter II.
  4. Verbs and commas. An action verb that lands, and every comma doing a job.
